description: Expected API paths from a single-stage `vespasian scan` of the REST API target (LAB-3890 T2, gap A1). Consumed by test_scan_rest in test/run-live-tests.sh. Unlike rest-api (two-stage crawl + `generate rest --probe=false`), this exercises the scan command's full pipeline end-to-end with the HEADLESS browser and active probing on. /api/subscribe is served ONLY as a static HTML <form> action (never linked or fetched), so its presence proves the analyze.ExtractForms augmentation ran inside scan. Parameter names may vary ({userId} vs {id}); validate_path_coverage matches params positionally. PARTIAL LOCKSTEP WITH expected-paths.json — the two fixtures are kept identical on the path SET, total_paths, post_form_paths, and post_form_body_fields_by_path (exactly the fields _assert_fixture_parity in test/validate_test.sh compares), so any endpoint added to or removed from the test/rest-api server MUST be applied to BOTH files or that assertion fails loudly. They DELIBERATELY DIVERGE on the per-path method lists for /api/login and /api/upload: here both are GET+POST, in expected-paths.json both are GET-only. This is real generator behavior, not drift — test_scan_rest runs the headless `scan` (JavaScript executes, firing the inline `fetch('/api/login',{method:'POST'})` / `fetch('/api/upload',{method:'POST'})` calls) with active probing on, so both paths are observed as GET+POST. test_rest_api generates from the non-headless http capture with `--probe=false`: no JS runs and no probe fires, so the same POST literals are recovered statically as GET-only candidates (Source=static:js, floored to default confidence by RESTClassifier Rule 7) and surface GET-only there. /api/subscribe is POST in both files because it originates from the static <form> via ExtractForms, independent of JS execution. The method lists are intentionally NOT compared by _assert_fixture_parity, and validate_path_coverage reads path keys only, so this divergence is expected and asserted-around rather than enforced. Whoever changes the two-stage vs scan discovery behavior (e.g. adds a probe/discovery stage to one command, or removes it) should update these method lists and this note in both files to match.
